1353. 12. Februar. Auinione. — Papst Innocem VI. beauftragt den Erzbischof von Prag, dem Weltpriester Mauritz von Malenitz zu irgend einem Beneficium, dessen Präsentation dem Abte and Convente zu Hohenfurt zusteht, zu verhelfen. 1353. 14. Juni. Prag. — liartholomäus und Stephan, Domherren der Prager Kirche und vicarii in spiritualibus des Erzbischofes Arnest von Prag, beauftra gen den Dedrant von Teindles und die Pfarrer von Priethal und Rosenberg mit der Vollziehung vorstehender Dulle des Papstes Innocenz VI. 1353. 14. Juni. 0. �?0. — ¡wein von Klosterneuburg mit mehreren seiner Ver wandten kauft вон dem Abte Heinrich von Hohenfurt und dem dortigen Convente fünf Viertheile Weingärten, gelegen am Puchberg, um acht Pfund Wiener Pfenninge.

XCIX. Innocencius episcopus seruus seruorum dei venerabili fratri archiepiscopo Pragensi salutem et apostolicam benedictionem. Con- stitutus in presencia nostra dilectus filius Mauricius natus quondam Petri de Malenicz pauper presbyter tue dyocesis nobis humiliter supplicauit, ut cum ipse, sicut asserit, beneficium aliquod ecclesia- stieum non obtineat, prouideri sibi de benignitate apostolica manda- remus. Quia igitur illi sunt ad ecclesiastica beneficia promouendi, quibus mores et sciencia suffragantur; cum idem presbyter, quem per certos examinatores super hoc deputatos a nobis de litteratura examinari fecimus diligenter, inuentus sit in illa conuenienter ydoneus ad ecclesiasticum beneficium obtinendum, nos de uita et conuersa- cione ipsius presbyteri noticiam non habenies fraternitati tue per apostolica scripta mandamus, quatinus de hiis solerter inquirens, si enim vite laudabilis et honeste conuersacionis esse reperies, et aliud ecclesiasticum beneficium non obtineat, aliudque canonicum non ob- sistat, et de aliquo ecclesiastico beneficio secundum sue probitatis merita competenti cum cura uel sine cura consueto ab olim clericis secularibus assignari spectante communiter uel diuisim ad collacio- nem uel presentacionem dilectorum filiorum abbatis et conuentus monasterii in Altouado Cisterciensis ordinis dicte dyocesis, si quod in ciuitate uel dyocesi Pragensi uacat ad presens, uel quam primum ad id obtulerit se facultas, per te uel alium seu alios prouidere pro cures, induceos eum in corporalem ppssessionem eiusdem benefici i et defendons inductum ac faciens ipsum ad illud, si in ecclesia col- legiata secundum disticcionem (sic) nostram inferius annotatam ex- titerit, postquam de ipso uacante sibi prouisum fuerit, ¡n canonicum recipi et in fratrem. Non obstante si aliqui nostra uel predecessorum nostrorum Romanorum pontificum auctoritate huiusmodi beneficia ad dictorum abbatis et conuentus collacionëm uel presentacionem spec- tancia tam in huiusmodi pauperum quam alia quacumque forma proui- sionis expectent, quibus omnibus preterquam auctoritate nostra huius modi beneficia expectantibus dictum presbyterum in assecucione huiusmodi beneficii uolumus anteferri, sed nullum per hoc eis quo ad assecucionem aliorum beneficiorum preiudicium generari; aut si ali- quibus de beneficiis ecclesiasticis ad dictos abbatem et conuentum spectantibus per nostras litteras sit prouisum, seu si eisdem abbati et conuentui uel personis ipsius ecclesie, in qua sibi prouideri con- tigerit, a sede apostolica sit indultum, quod ad recepcionem uel prouisionem aJicuius minime teneantur, quodque ad id compelli aut quod interdici suspendi uel excommunicari non possint, uel quod de beneficiis ad eorum collacionem uel presentacionem spectantibus non possit aliquibus prouideri, per lilteras apostolicas non facientes ple num et expressam de indulto huismodi mencionem sine qualibet alia prefate sedis indulgencia, cuiuscumque- tenoris existat, per quam effectus presencium impediri valeat uel differi, et de qua in nostris litteris mencionem fieri oporteat specialem, contradictores per cen- suram ecclesiasticam appellacione posposita compescendo. Ita tamen quod idem presbyter, prout requiret onus benefieii, de quo ei proui sum fuerit, personaliter resideat in eodem, mandatum nostrum in hac parte ¡mpleturus, quod in eo impendisse lauderis misericordiam pau- peri et obedienciam mandatori. Volumus autem, quod omnes alie littere a sede predicta uel eius legatis seu quibuslibet aliis obtente necnon promissiones et obligaciones a quibuscumque personis facte super ipsius presbyteri prouisione sint inualide omnique careat (sic) firmitate. Ceterum districcius inhibemus, ne prefato presbytero auc- toritate presencium in cathedrali aliquatenus prouideatur ecclesia uel de cuiuslibet ecclesie collegiate prebenda uel alio ecclesiastico bene ficio sine cura, cuius redditus et prouentus annui quindecim marcha- rum argenti summam siue de aliqua parrochiali ecclesia uel aliquo ecclesiastico beneficio curam animarum habente, cuius redditus et prouentus viginti marcharum argenti annuam quantitatem excedant, valorem autem annuum buiusmodi reddituum et prouentuum declara- mus et haberi volumus extimatum (sic), prout de illis secundum ta- xacionem uel alias pro decima est amplius persolutum. Nostre tamen intencionis existit, quod de huiusmodi beneficio eeiam, si minoris. quam predicitur, valoris extiterit, possit eidem presbytero, si illud infra vnius mensis spacium, postquam sibi de ipsius beneficii uaca- cione constiterit, acceptare uoluerit, prouideri. Prefatis enim abbati et conuentui, ne post insinuacionem presencium et processuum per eas habitorum eis factam de ipso beneficio interim eciam ante accep 102 tacionem huiusmodi disponere quoquo modo presumant, districcius inhibemus, decernentes irritum et inane, si secus super premissis a quoquam quauis anctoritate contigerit attemptari. Datum Auinione II. Idus Februarii pontificatus nostri anno primo. Inserirt ¡n die Urkunde N. C. С. 1353. 14. Juni. Prag. — liartholomäus und Stephan, Domherren der Prager Kirche und vicarii in spiritualibus des Erzbischofes Arnest von Prag, beauftra gen den Dedrant von Teindles und die Pfarrer von Priethal und Rosenberg mit der Vollziehung vorstehender Dulle des Papstes Innocenz VI. Bartholomeus, decanus ecclesie sancti Egidii maioris ciuilatis Pragensis, et Stephanus canonici Pragensis ecclesie, reuerendissimi in Christo patris et domini domini Arnesti dei et epostolice sedis gratia sanete ecclesie Pragensis archiepiscopi executons principalis ad infrascripta a sede .apostolica deputati vicarii in spiritualibus ge nerales, venerabilibus ac religiosis viris abbati et conuentui mona- sterii in Altouado ordinis Cisterciensis Pragensis diocesis ac omnibus et singulis, ad quos presentes littero peruenerint et quos infrascripta contingunt seu contingere poterunt, quoquo modo quocumque no mine censeantur. salutem in domino et inandatis nostris ymo verius apostolicis humiliter obedire. Lilteras sanctissimi in Christo patris et domini nostri domini Innocencii diuina prouidencia pape VI'1 eius vera bulla plumbea cum cordula canapis bullatas sanas et integras omnique suspicione carentes presentatas nobis per discretum virum, Mauricium de Malenicz presbiterum eiusdem dyocesis nos cum ea, qua decuit, reuerencia recepisse noueritis sub hac forma: [Folgt die Bulle des Papstes Innocens VI., ausgestellt zu Auinione 1353. 12. Februar. (N. XCIX.)]. Post quarum litter'arum apostolicarum presentacionem et lecturam predictus Mauricius presbyter nobis humiliter supplicauit, ut dictum mandatum apostolicum predicto domino nostro archiepis- copo Pragensi in hac parte commissum vice et nomine ipsius execu- toris nobis in hac parte commissum exsecucioni debite mandaremus. Nos igitur vicarii prefati tamquam obediencie filii volentes mandatum apostolicum predictum exsequi reuerenter auctoritate apostolica, qua fungimur in hac parte, de vita et eonuersacione ipsius presbyteri et aliis circumstanciis in ipsis litteris apostolicis contenus iuxta traditam nobis formam in quisiuimus diligenter, et quia ipsum ex fide digno 103 rum testimonio vite laudabilis et honeste conuersacionis esse repe- rrmus nee inuenimus aliquod canonicum, quod obstet eidem, propter quod dicta prouisio retardan uel impediri deberet, ipsum pronunc- ciamus abilem et idoneum ad ecclesiastieum beneficium obtinendum vsque ad ualorem et summam in eisdem litteris apostolicis compre- hensam. Ideoque ecclesiastieum beneficium nulli alii de iure debitum cum cura uel sine cura eidem presbytero sibi tamen competens se- cundum sue probitatis merita spectans ad collacionem uel presenta- cionem vestram, si quod in ciuitate uel dyocesi Pragensi vacat, ad presens consuetum ab olim clericis secularibus assignari, cuius redditus annui summam viginti marcarum cum cura uel sine cura quindecim secundum taxacionem in prefatis litteris apostolicis con- tentam non excedant, quod idem presbyter per se uel procuratorem suum ad hoc legittime constitutum infra vnius mensis spacium a noti cia vacacionis ipsius duxerit acceptandum, cum omnibus iuribus et pertinenciis suis auctoritate apostolica conferimus et eidem de ipso prouidemus, ipsumpue per birretum nostrum inuestimus de eodem. Vosque abbatem et conuentum necnon omnes et singulos alios, quo rum interest uel interesse poterit, primo secundo tercio et peremp- torie requirimus et monemus communiter et diuisim vobis nichilomi- nus in virtute sanete obediencie precipiendo mandantes, quatinus infra sex dies a presentacione seu notificacione presencium vobis facta, quorum duos pro primo pro secundo et reliquos duos vobis et aliis, quorum interest uel interesse poterit, pro tercio et peremptorie termino ac monicione canonica assignamus eundem presbyterum uel suum procuratorem eius nomine ad dictum beneficium, de quo sibi prouidimus, sine difficultate qualibet recipiatis et eciam ad- mittatis, permitientes ipsum pacifica ipsius beneficii possessione gaudere, amouentes ab eo quemlibet illicitum et iniustum detentorem, quem et nos exnunc prout extunc amouemus, sibique uel eius procu ratori pro eo de ipsius beneficii fructibus redditibus prouentibus e obuencionibus vniuersis, prout ad uos pertinet, faciatis integre res- ponderi. Quod si dictum beneficium, de quo sibi prouidimus, in ecclesia collegiata existat, eundem presbyterum uel procuratorem suum eius nomine infra predictum terminum, prout ipsius beneficii qualitas exigit, in canonicum et in fratrem ipsius ecclesie recipiatis et recipi ab aliis faciatis, stallum in choro et locum in capitulo ipsius ecclesie, ut moris est, cum omni plenitudine iuris canonici sibi uel 104 procuratori suo pro eo assignando. Si uero tempore date (sic) pre- scncium nullum beneficium tale cum cura uel sine cura ad vestram, domine abba et conuentus, collacionem seu prouisionem pertinens in ciuitate uel dyocesi predictis vaeabat (sic), nos beneficium simile ac eciam beneficium minoris valoris, si dictus presbyter huiusmodi beneficium infra vnius mensis spacium, postquam sibi de ipsius be nefici i vacacione constiterit, acceptare voluerit, in ciuitate uel dyo cesi supradictis proximo uacaturum conferendum eidem presbytèro cum omnibus iuribus et pertinenciis suis collacioni nostre et cuilibet subdelegatorum nostrorum infrascriptorum ymo pocius apostolice reseruamus, districcius inbibentes vobis abbati et couuentui predicto ac omnibus aliis, quorum interest uel intererit, ne huiusmodi bene ficium per nos dicto presbytero collatum uel conferendum, ut pre- mittitur, reseruatum alicui alii conferatis, seu ad ipsum quemquam alium presentetis, aut de ¡По uel aliquo iure ad ipsum beneficium quomodolibet pertinente in preiudicium dicti presbyteri quomodolibet disponatis, ac decernentes exnunc irritum et inane, si secus super hiis a quoquam quauis auctoritate scienter uel ignoranter contigerit attemptari prefatas quoque litteras et hune nostrum processum ac omnia et singula instrumenta et litteras dicti presbyteri negocium huiusmodi contingencia; si et quando ad nos peruenerint, retenta ipsorum copia, si eam habere voluentis, quam vobis fieri decernimus vestris tamen sumptibus et expensis, eidem presbytero uel procura tori suo pro eo, cum super hoc ab eis uel eorum altero requisiti fueritis, sine difficultate qualibet resjjtuatis integra et illesa sub pena supertus expressa ac aliis predictis et infrascriptis nostris monicioni- bus et mandatis plenarie obedire studeatis. Quod si forte, quod ab- sit, premissa omnia et singula, prout ad uos et singulos vestrum per tinent, non adimpleueritis aut aliquid in contrarium feceritis uel monicionibus et mandatis nostris huiusmodi ymo verius apostolicis in hac parte non parueritis cum effectu, in vos dominum abbatem et conuentum predictum et contradictores quoslibet et rebelles ac dictum presbyterum quomodolibet impedientes super premissis aut in aliquo impedientibus ipsum dantes consilium auxilium uel fauorem publice uel occulte directe uel indirecte, cuiuscumque status ordinis gradus preeminencie dignitatis auctoritatis seu condicionis existant, exnunc singulariter et in singulis predicta monicione canonica premissa ex- communicacionis sententiam ferimus in biis scriptis absolucione om 105 nium et singulorum, qui predictas et infrascriptas nostras ymo pocius apostolicas sentencias uel earum aliquam iucurrerint, quoquomodo nobis uel superiori nosíro preterquam in mortis articulo tantummodo reseruantes. Ceterum cum ad exsecucionem huiusmodi vlterius f;ici- endum non possumus quo ad presens personaliter interesse, venera- bilihus et discretis viris decano Dudlebensi plebano ecclesie in Rosenberch et plebano ecclesie in Pryedal, quibus et eorum cuilibet in solidum super exsecucione predicti mandati apostolici atque nostri tenore presencium committimus vices nostras, donec eas ad nos du- xerimus reuocandas, quos et quemlibet ipsorum monemus primo secundo et tercio et peremptorie in virtute sanete obediencie et sub excommunicacionis pena, quam predicta canonica municione premissa ¡n eos et eorum quemlibet ferimus in biis scriptis, si ea que ipsis et eorum cuilibet in hac parte committimus, neglexerint seu coniemp- serint contumaciter, adimplere districte precipiendo mandamus, qua- tenus ipsi et eorum quilibet vnus alium non expectans, qui predietum presbyterum uel eius procuratorem super hoc requisiti fuerint, infra sex dies a requisicione huiusmodi inmediate sequentes, quos eis pro omnibus dilacionibus ac monicione canonica assignamus ad vos do- minum abbatem et conuentum predictum necnon ad omnes et singulos, quorum interest uel interesse poterit, quoquomodo personaliter acce dant et predictas litteras apostolicas et hunc nostrum processum ac omnia et singula in eis contenta vobis et aliis, quorum interest uel intererit, in predicto monasterio et extra et alios, vbi quando et quoeiens expediens fuerit, denunccient legant et publicare procurent et prefatum presbyterum uel procuratorem suum eius nomine corpo- ralem possessionem beneficii per nos, ut premittitur, sibi collati ju- rium et pertinenciarum eius. Si quod tempore collacionis huiusmodi per nos sibi facte vacabat, inducant et defendent inductum amoto abinde quolibet illicita detentore alioquin beneficium per nos, ut permittitur, reseruatum, cum illud vacare contigerit, eidem presby- tero cum omnibus iuribus et pertinenciis suis conferant et assignent ipsumque facian t pacifica illorum possessione gaudere. Et si illud beneficium in ecclesia collegiata fuerit, eundem presbyterum uel procuratorem suum pro eo in eadem ecclesia recipi faciant in cano- nicum et in fratrem, stallo sibi in choro et loco in capitulo ipsius ecclesie cum plenitudine iuris canonici assignatis, sibique uel dicto procuratori suo pro eo de ipsius beneficii fructibus redditibus prouen 106 (¡bus iuribus et obuencionibus vniuersis integre responderi, ac alias in omnibus et singulis pertinentibus ad exsecucionem huismodi gracie procedant libere vice nostra. Ita tamen, quod in preiudicium dicti presbyteri nichil valeant attemptare nee in processibus nee in sen- tenciis per nos habitis atque latis absoluendo uel suspendendo ali- quatinus immutare volumus; insuper vt, quod per aliquem dictorum subdelegatorum nostrorum ceptum fuerit, per alium seu alios possit terminari. Et si contingat, nos vlterius super premissis procedere non intendimus commissionem buiusmodi in aliquo reuocare, nisi de reuocacione ipsius plena et expressa in litteris reuocatoriis mencio habeatur. In quorum omnium testimonium et pleniorem roboris fir- mitatem presentes litteras siue hunc nostrum processum fieri et sigilio nostri vicariatus fecimus appensione muniri. Ich Ybein ze Neunburch chlosterhalb vnd ich Elzpet sein haus- vraw vnd ich Jacob sein bruder vnd ich Elzpet sein hausvraw vnd ich Hainrich der vargenanten paiden brueder vnd ich Katrey sein hausvraw vnd ich Weygand zden czeiten Ybeins hofherre vnd ich Tristram vnd all vnser eriben vergehen vnd tun chunt mit disem brief offenleichen, daz wir all vnuerschaidenleichen gelten sullen dem erbirdigen gestleichem herren hern Hainreichen zden czeiten apt vnd dem conuent gemayn ze Hohenfuert acht phunt Wienner phen- ninge, do sy vns mit verayntem willen fumf virtayl weingarten ze chauffen vmb gegeben habent vnd liegent in dem Puchperige ze- nachst Lyenharten von Eybesprunne, do man von dient drey emmer 107 weins vnd drey stauff ze perchrecht vnd dritdhalb phenninge ze voitrecht vnd nicht mer. Wir sullen auch in von den egenanten acht phunten dienn alle iar ayu phunt an sand Merteins tage in irn hofe ge Nusdorf, wer do ir verweser ist, mit alle den nuczen vnd rechten alz man ander purchrecht dient in Osterrich. Tun wir des nicht, so sol sich der selb dienst ye vber virczehen tage dar nach zwispilden, alz ander versezzen dienst recht ist. Wir seczen in auch payde fur di acht phunt vnd dienst vnd zwispild ze phant di egenanten fumf virtayl Weingarten mit vnser aller gutleichem willen vnd mit vnsers perigmaister hant hern Wysenten auf dem Anger zden czeiten ampt- man hern Rudolfotten von Lychtenstayn vnd sein auch wir alle des gelben phunt geltes auf den egenanten fumf virtayl weingarten recht gewern vnd scherm, alz landes recht ist vnd perchrechtes recht in Osterrich, vnd waz dem conuent gemayn dar an abget, daz sullen sy haben auf vns vargenanten allen vnuerschaidlichen ab aynem auf dem andern vnd auf alle dem, daz wir haben, wir sein lebentig oder tode. Wir haben auch recht vnd vreywal, swann wir mugen oder wellen im iar, swelher der ist vnder vns, der do geit sein tayl awz den acht phunten, waz in anpuert vnd den dienst darauf, so ist er ledich vnd vrey awz disem brief an all Widerrede, vnd sullen im des di herren oder ir anwalt stat tun. Vnd geben darvber dem egenantem hern Hainreichen dem apt vnd dem conuent gemain ze Hohenfuert disen brief versigilten mit vnsers egenanten perigmaister insigil hern Wysenten auf dem Anger vnd mit des erbern mannes insigil hern Jacobs seines bruder czdeu czeiten statrichter, den wir zu diser sache ze geczeugen peten haben. Der brief ist geben nach Christ purd dreuczehen hundert iar vnd im dreu vnd fumfzgisten iar an sand Veytes abent. Zwei kleine, an Pergamentstreifen hängende Siegel in weissem Wachs, beide beschädigt. a) Ein Schild mi't zwei kreuzweis übereinander liegenden Fischen. — . . Wisentonis . Filii . Clavigi . . b) Ein Schild mit demselben Abzeichen. — f S . Jac . . . Filii . Cla . . . 108 CIL 1353. 15. August. 0. A0. — Abt Albert von Hohenfurt bestimmt zur Sicherslel- lung einer seinem Convente schuldigen Summe die Einkünfte von seinen Gütern in Luppetschnig. Ne gesta causarum ac rerum annositas annorum dierumve diu- turnitas prolixa ab htbili memoria hominum euanescant et pereant, prvdencia solet ea virorum discretorum per litteras eternare. Nos igitur frater Albertus dictus abbas in Altovado ad perpetue rei me- moriam presentibus publicamus et declaramus, quod noster gratiosus olim fundator commemoracionis felicis dominus Petrus de Rosenberch inter cetera caritatis pietatisque opera multa et bona, que nobis atque monasterio nostro inpendit et ostendit, eciam nobis et conuen- tui nostro donauit ac dedit ob remedium anime dilecti amici sui Johannis de Dobruscha pie memorie centum sexagenas grossorum promptorum monete Pragensis specifice tamen et condicionaliter, vt videlicet de quinquaginta sexagenis denariorum perhenniter singulis annis agatur in nostro conuentu sui anniuersarius dies cum missis orationibus specialibus iuxta commendabilem nostri ordinis morem, et die eodem conuentui in refectorium etiam de predicta pecunia debet prandium dari ex prouidencia caritateque domini abbatis, qui est vel futurus est, de reliquis vero quinquaginta sexagenis a came rario nostre dormis, qui est vel pro tempore fuerit, omnibus perpetue annis toti conuentui fratribus et monachis vniuersis noue tunice de- bent dari, vnicuique fratri tunicam vnam, melius prout vestiarius ex prouisone comparare poterit. Hanc autem summum pecunie supra- dictam recepit in sua, qui protunc abbatizauit, deuote recordacionis dominus Thomas abbas buius loci, et in necessarios vsus monasterii impendit et congregacioni pro eadem pecunia inpensa et consumpta, ne in posterum suo vestitu atque solacio per aliquem successorul!i suorum priuaretur, deputauit et obligauit paterna ex caritate vnam decimam in Pryedal, donec satisfaceret conuentui in prelocutapecunia refundenda, videlicet in quinquaginta sexagenis denariorum grosso rum Prageusium, de quibus quinquaginta sexagenis denariorum ex- soluit et satisfecit, dum adhuc viueret, camere xx" libras denariorum Patauiensium. Pro ceteris vero denariis nos ad preces et instanciam consilium atque communem voluntatem tocius nostri conuentus pro supradicta decima damus ac perpctuamus imperpetuum domus nostre 109 camere certos annuos redditus in bonis nostris in Lvppulsching quin que talenta denariorum Wyennensis Patauiensisve monete et xxli denarios, quos vestiarius ipse domus nostre, qui est vel fuerit, colli- gere et recipere debet per singulos annos et conuentui prouidere de vestitu suo absque hominis cuiuslibet obstaculo contradiccione vel impedimento, sicuti est superius diffinitum. In cuius rei cautelam memoriamque perpetuam ac euidens testimonium sigillari iussimus paginas presentes nostri videlicet ac conuentus nostri sigillo necnon reuerendi domini ;ic patris abbatis atque visitatoris nostri sigillo de Hylaria et nostri eciam generosi ac gratiosi fvndatoris nostri sigillo domini Petri de Rosenberch. Datum actumque anno verbi incarnati millesimo trecentesimo quinquagesimo tercio in die assumpeionis beate Marie virginis. Altova . . b) Dos Siegel des Hohenfurter Conventes in weis- sem Wachs, beschädigt, dessen nähere Beschreibung bei CXL. c) Ziemlich gross, in weissem Wachs. — Abt mit Krummstab und Buch. — -j- S . Wern- hardi . Abbatis . In . Wilhering. Das Siegel Peters von Rosenberg ist nicht mehr vorhanden.

1353, 12 February. Avignon. — Pope Innocent VI commissions the Archbishop of Prague to provide the secular priest Mauritz von Malenitz with some benefice whose presentation belongs to the abbot and convent of Hohenfurt. 1353, 14 June. Prague. — Bartholomew and Stephan, canons of the Prague church and vicars in spiritual matters of Archbishop Arnest of Prague, commission Dedrant of Teindles and the parish priests of Priethal and Rosenberg to execute the foregoing bull of Pope Innocent VI. 1353, 14 June. Undated place. — Ywein of Klosterneuburg, with several of his relatives, buys from Abbot Heinrich of Hohenfurt and its convent five quarter vineyard plots on Puchberg for eight pounds of Viennese pennies.

XCIX. Innocent, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother, the Archbishop of Prague: greeting and apostolic blessing. Our beloved son Mauricius, son of the late Petrus of Malenicz, a poor priest of your diocese, appeared before us and humbly petitioned that, since, as he asserts, he holds no ecclesiastical benefice, we should by apostolic kindness order provision to be made for him. Since those whose character and learning support them are to be promoted to ecclesiastical benefices, and since the same priest, whom we had carefully examined in learning through examiners appointed by us for this purpose, was found suitably qualified to obtain an ecclesiastical benefice, we, having no knowledge of his life and conduct, command your fraternity by apostolic letters to inquire diligently into these matters. If you find him to be of commendable life and honest conduct, if he holds no other ecclesiastical benefice, if no other canonical impediment exists, and if there is a suitable ecclesiastical benefice, with or without cure of souls, according to his merits, of the kind customarily assigned to secular clerics, belonging jointly or separately to the collation or presentation of our beloved sons the abbot and convent of the Cistercian monastery at Hohenfurt in the said diocese, and if one is now vacant in the city or diocese of Prague or opportunity for it arises as soon as possible, then take care to provide it to him, through yourself or another or others; induct him into its corporeal possession and defend him once inducted. If it is in a collegiate church, after provision of the vacant benefice to him, have him received as a canon and brother, according to our distinction set out below. Notwithstanding that some may expect such benefices belonging to the collation or presentation of the said abbot and convent by authority of ourselves or our predecessors, the Roman pontiffs, whether in this or any other form of provision, we wish this priest to be preferred in obtaining this benefice over all those expecting such benefices by any authority other than ours, without prejudice thereby to their obtaining other benefices; or notwithstanding that provision may have been made by our letters to anyone in benefices belonging to the said abbot and convent, or that the Apostolic See may have granted to the abbot and convent or persons of the church in which provision is made that they need not admit or provide anyone, and cannot be compelled to do so or be interdicted, suspended, or excommunicated, or that no one may be provided in benefices of their collation or presentation, unless apostolic letters make full and express mention of such an indult, without any other indulgence of the said See, of whatever tenor, whose effect might impede or delay these presents and which would need special mention in our letters. Compel any dissenters by ecclesiastical censure, without appeal. The priest must reside personally in the benefice provided to him, as its burden requires, thereby fulfilling our mandate and earning praise for showing mercy to a poor man and obedience to the one giving the command. We also wish all other letters obtained from the said See or its legates or any others, and all promises and obligations made by any persons concerning provision for this priest, to be invalid and without force. Moreover, we strictly forbid provision by authority of these presents to the said priest in a cathedral church, to a prebend or other benefice without cure of souls in any collegiate church whose annual income exceeds fifteen silver marks, or to a parish church or other benefice with cure of souls whose annual income exceeds twenty silver marks. The annual value of such income is to be assessed as the amount from which the greater sum was paid in tithes, according to its valuation or otherwise. It is, however, our intention that even a benefice of lesser value may be provided to him if he wishes to accept it within one month after learning of its vacancy. We strictly forbid the aforesaid abbot and convent, after receiving notice of these presents and the proceedings held under them, from disposing in any way in the meantime of the benefice before such acceptance. We decree null and void anything anyone may attempt otherwise in these matters, under any authority. Given at Avignon, on 12 February, in the first year of our pontificate. Inserted in charter no. C.

[The following item, dated 14 June 1353, records the execution of the papal mandate. Bartholomeus, dean of the church of St Giles in the greater city of Prague, and Stephan, canons of the Prague church, principal executors appointed for the matters below by the Apostolic See and vicars general in spiritual matters of the most reverend father and lord Arnest, by the grace of God and the Apostolic See Archbishop of Prague, to the venerable and religious men, the abbot and convent of the monastery at Hohenfurt of the Cistercian order in the diocese of Prague, and to all others whom these matters concern or may concern, whatever their designation: greetings in the Lord, and humble obedience to our commands, or rather to apostolic commands. Know that we received with due reverence the letters of our most holy father in Christ and lord, Pope Innocent VI, sealed with his true leaden bull on a hemp cord, presented to us by the discreet man Mauricius of Malenicz, priest of the same diocese, whole, intact, and beyond suspicion, in the following form: [The bull of Pope Innocent VI, issued at Avignon on 12 February 1353, follows above (no. XCIX).] After presentation and reading of those apostolic letters, the priest Mauricius humbly petitioned us to carry out the apostolic mandate entrusted in this matter to our lord Archbishop of Prague, as executor, in his place and name. We, the aforesaid vicars, as sons of obedience, wishing reverently to execute the apostolic mandate by the authority entrusted to us for this matter, diligently inquired into the priest’s life and conduct and the other circumstances contained in the apostolic letters, according to the form prescribed to us. On the trustworthy testimony of witnesses, we found him to be of commendable life and honest conduct, and found no canonical impediment that should delay or prevent the provision. We therefore declare him able and qualified to obtain an ecclesiastical benefice up to the value specified in those apostolic letters. Accordingly, we confer upon this priest and provide him with an ecclesiastical benefice, due to no one else by right and suitable to him according to his merits, with or without cure of souls, customarily assigned of old to secular clerics and belonging to your collation or presentation, if one is now vacant in the city or diocese of Prague, whose annual income does not exceed twenty marks if with cure of souls, or fifteen if without, according to the assessment stated in the apostolic letters, and which the priest or his duly constituted representative chooses to accept within one month of learning of its vacancy; and we invest him with it by our cap. We jointly and individually require and admonish you, abbot and convent, and all others concerned, first, second, third, and finally, and command you under holy obedience that within six days of receiving or being notified of these presents (two days assigned for the first, two for the second, and the remaining two as the third and final canonical warning) you receive and admit the priest, or his representative in his name, to the benefice provided for him without difficulty, allow him peaceful possession, remove any unlawful or unjust holder from it (whom we hereby remove now for then), and cause him or his representative to receive in full the fruits, revenues, proceeds, and perquisites of the benefice, as falls to your responsibility. If the benefice is in a collegiate church, within the aforesaid term receive the priest or his representative in his name as a canon and brother of that church, as the nature of the benefice requires, and assign him a stall in the choir and a place in the chapter with the full rights of canon law. If at the date of these presents no benefice of this kind, with or without cure of souls, belonging to the collation or provision of you, the abbot and convent, is vacant in the aforesaid city or diocese, we reserve to our own collation and to that of any of our subdelegates below—indeed, rather, to apostolic provision—the next similar benefice to become vacant in the said city or diocese, including one of lesser value if the priest wishes to accept it within one month after learning of the vacancy, to be conferred upon him with all its rights and appurtenances. We strictly forbid you, the said abbot and convent, and all others concerned now or in future to confer on anyone else, present anyone else to, or otherwise dispose to the prejudice of the said priest of any benefice conferred on him by us or reserved for him as aforesaid, or of any right belonging to it. We decree now that any contrary act, knowingly or unknowingly, by anyone under any authority shall be null and void. We further direct that the aforesaid apostolic letters, this our process, and all instruments and letters concerning the priest’s matter that come into our hands shall be returned to him or his representative, intact and without difficulty, upon request by either of them, retaining a copy if you wish, to be made at your own cost; and that you carefully obey fully and without difficulty the foregoing and subsequent warnings and commands, under the aforesaid penalty. If, which may it not be, you fail to carry out any or all of the foregoing matters falling to you, or do anything contrary to them, or fail effectively to obey these warnings and commands, which are rather apostolic, then, having first given the canonical warning stated above, we hereby in writing pronounce sentence of excommunication against you, the said abbot and convent, and any dissenters or rebels, and anyone in any way impeding the said priest in these matters, or giving advice, aid, or favor to anyone impeding him, openly or secretly, directly or indirectly, whatever their status, order, rank, pre-eminence, dignity, authority, or condition. We reserve to ourselves or our superior the absolution of each and every person who incurs any of the foregoing or subsequent sentences, except only at the point of death. Since we cannot at present be personally present to take further steps in execution of this matter, by these presents we entrust our authority to the venerable and discreet men, the dean of Dudlebs, the parish priest of Rosenberg, and the parish priest of Pryedal, and to each of them individually, until we revoke it. We admonish them, first, second, third, and finally, under holy obedience and on pain of excommunication (which we hereby pronounce in writing against them, after the aforesaid canonical warning, if they contumaciously neglect or refuse the matters entrusted to them), and strictly command them that, without waiting for one another, within six days immediately following a request from the priest or his representative, a period assigned for all delays and as canonical warning, they personally approach you, the aforesaid abbot and convent, and all others concerned, and announce, read, and publish to you and them the apostolic letters and our process and everything contained therein, at the monastery and elsewhere, wherever and whenever expedient. They shall induct the said priest or his representative in his name into corporeal possession of the benefice, with its rights and appurtenances, if it was vacant when we conferred it, and defend him in possession, removing any unlawful holder; otherwise, when the benefice reserved by us becomes vacant, they shall confer and assign it to the priest with all its rights and appurtenances and ensure his peaceful possession. If the benefice is in a collegiate church, they shall arrange for the priest or his representative to be received there as a canon and brother, with a stall in the choir and a place in the chapter assigned with the full rights of canon law; they shall ensure that the fruits, revenues, proceeds, rights, and all perquisites of the benefice are paid to him or his representative in full, and shall freely proceed in our place in all matters pertaining to execution of this grace. They shall do nothing to prejudice the priest or alter in any way the proceedings and sentences we have issued, by absolving or suspending them. We further wish that whatever one of the said subdelegates begins may be completed by another or others. We do not intend to revoke this commission unless the revocation is fully and expressly mentioned in the revocation letters. In witness and fuller confirmation of all these matters, we have caused these letters, or this process, to be made and sealed with the seal of our vicariate. Given at Prague in the year of the Lord 1353, on 14 June. In the upper left corner of the charter, in a hand other than that of the charter scribe: “O Jur.” Damaged, rather large seal of white wax hanging from parchment strips: St Wenceslas, with a shield bearing a crossbar to his right and a shield bearing the forepart of a horse to his left; two priests kneel at the saint’s feet. Inscription: “Seal of the Vicariate of the Bishop … of Prague.”

CI. 1353, 14 June, undated place. — Ywein of Klosterneuburg buys five quarter vineyard plots on Puchberg for eight pounds of Viennese pennies from Abbot Heinrich of Hohenfurt and its convent, together with several relatives.

I, Ywein of Klosterneuburg on the monastery side, and I, Elzpet, his wife, and I, Jacob, his brother, and I, Elzpet, his wife, and I, Heinrich, brother of the aforesaid couple, and I, Katrey, his wife, and I, Weygand, at that time Ywein’s steward, and I, Tristram, and all our heirs, jointly acknowledge and make known by this open charter that we shall all be jointly liable to the venerable spiritual lord, Lord Heinrich, then abbot, and the community of Hohenfurt for eight pounds of Viennese pennies, for which they have by mutual agreement sold us five quarter vineyard plots on Puchberg, beside the property of Lyenhart of Eybesprunne. Three buckets of wine and three stauf are owed from them as vineyard dues, and two and a half pennies as vogt dues, and no more. Each year we shall pay them one pound of the aforesaid eight pounds on St Martin’s Day at their court at Nussdorf, to whoever is then their steward, with all the benefits and rights by which other vineyard dues are paid in Austria. If we fail to do this, the due shall double every fourteen days thereafter, as is the law for overdue dues. With the good will of us all and with the consent of our vineyard master, Lord Wysent auf dem Anger, then bailiff of Lord Rudolf von Lichtenstein, we pledge the aforesaid five quarter vineyard plots as security for the eight pounds, dues, and doubling thereof. We shall all jointly warrant and defend against all claims that yearly pound of rent on the aforesaid five quarter plots, as required by the law of the land and vineyard law in Austria. Whatever the community of the convent loses in this matter, it shall be able to recover jointly from all of us, one from another, and from all that we possess, whether we are living or dead. Any one of us may, whenever we can or wish during the year, pay his share of the eight pounds and the dues pertaining to him; he shall then be free and released from this charter without objection, and the lords or their agent shall give him formal quittance. In witness thereof we give this charter to the aforesaid Lord Heinrich, abbot, and the community of Hohenfurt, sealed with the seal of the aforesaid vineyard master, Lord Wysent auf dem Anger, and with the seal of the honorable man Lord Jacob, his brother, then town judge, whom we asked to witness this matter. The charter was given after the birth of Christ in the year 1353, on the eve of St Vitus. Two small, damaged seals in white wax hang from parchment strips: (a) a shield bearing two fish crossed over one another, inscription “... of Wysentonis, son of Clavigi”; (b) a shield with the same device, inscription “Seal of Jacob ... son of Cla...”.

CII. 1353, 15 August, undated place. — Abbot Albert of Hohenfurt assigns the revenues from his estates at Luppetschnig to secure a sum owed to his convent.

Lest the records of cases and affairs, through age and the long passage of years and days, fade and perish from the frail memory of people, the prudence of discreet men is accustomed to preserve them forever in writing. Therefore we, Brother Albert, called abbot at Hohenfurt, publish and declare by these presents for the perpetual memory of the matter that our gracious former founder, the late Lord Peter von Rosenberg, among the many good works of charity and piety that he bestowed and showed to us and our monastery, also gave and donated to us and our convent, for the remedy of the soul of his beloved friend John of Dobruscha, of pious memory, one hundred and fifty marks of current Prague groschen, specifically and conditionally as follows: from fifty marks of pennies, an annual anniversary for him is to be celebrated in perpetuity in our convent, with masses and special prayers according to the commendable custom of our order; on that day a meal is also to be provided to the convent in the refectory from this money, at the care and charitable discretion of the abbot then serving or to serve in future. From the remaining fifty marks, the cellarer of our house, now or in future, is to provide new tunics every year forever for all the brothers and monks of the convent, one tunic to each brother, of the best kind the wardrobe keeper can procure. The aforesaid sum of money was received by the late Lord Thomas, abbot of this place at the time, and spent on the necessary needs of the monastery. Out of fatherly charity, so that the community might not in future be deprived by one of his successors of the clothing and comfort provided by that money, he assigned and bound one tithe at Pryedal until he repaid the convent the aforesaid money expended, namely fifty marks of Prague groschen; from these fifty marks of pennies, while still alive, he paid and satisfied the treasury with twenty pounds of Passau pennies. For the remaining money, at the prayers and request, counsel, and common consent of our whole convent, we give and perpetually assign to the treasury of our house, in place of the aforesaid tithe, certain annual rents from our estates at Luppetschnig: five talents of Viennese or Passau pennies and twenty shillings, which the wardrobe keeper of our house, now or in future, is to collect and receive each year and use to provide the convent’s clothing, without obstruction, objection, or hindrance by anyone, as defined above. For security, perpetual remembrance, and clear testimony of this matter, we have ordered these present pages sealed with our seal and that of our convent, as well as the seal of the reverend lord and father, our abbot and visitor of Hilaria, and also the seal of our noble and gracious founder, Lord Peter von Rosenberg. Given and enacted in the year of the Incarnation of the Word 1353, on the feast of the Assumption of the Blessed Virgin Mary. Three seals hang from parchment strips: (a) damaged, moderately small seal in red wax, showing an abbot with crozier and book, inscription “... of Albert, Abbot ... of Hohenfurt”; (b) damaged seal of the Hohenfurt convent in white wax, described in detail under CXL; (c) rather large seal in white wax, showing an abbot with crozier and book, inscription “Seal of Wernhard, Abbot of Wilhering.” The seal of Peter von Rosenberg is no longer present.
